summary: groups.role_field names a membership-table column holding the member's IN-TENANT role (e.g. member_role on company_members: company_admin / project_manager / read_only_guest). The value joins the session's roles for the effective group, so `access: <table>: { update: role:company_admin }` enforces tenant roles declaratively - no parallel grant in _benmore_user_roles needed, and changing the column takes effect on the member's next request.
compose_with: access modes: role:<X> and role:<a>,<b> match membership-table roles exactly like platform roles on tables that carry the groups: key (bounded by the tenant clause). Admins still bypass. On a table WITHOUT the key column a tenant role does not pass a role: gate (only a global users.role or group_id-NULL grant does), except on the tenant root (groups.bootstrap.org_table), where it reaches only the caller's own tenant row: `companies: { update: role:company_admin }` lets an org's own admin edit that org, never another. The same holds for `perm:<res>.<action>` gates: a permission that only a tenant role grants does not pass one on a table without the key. Give a shared table the key column, list it in groups.shared, or use a global grant, when tenant members need it.

flows: `on.request.role: <name>` passes for a caller whose tenant role is that name (and for a global admin); the flow has no tenant column, so its SQL binds the tenant itself (`${{ user.group_id || 0 }}`). `role: admin` is the exception: only a global admin passes it, never a tenant role named admin - check the membership row in a flow step instead (api({at:'rbac'}) gotchas).

workflow transitions: `role: <name>` passes for a member whose tenant role is that name. `role: admin` passes for a tenant's admin only on a table that carries the groups: key (or is listed in groups.shared); on any other table only a global admin passes it (api({at:'workflows'}) transition_roles).

pages: a page's `role=` gate counts only roles held for the whole app, and a `{{#role "admin"}}` section opens for a global admin only; show a tenant admin's content with `{{#if user.app_role = "admin"}}` (api({at:'ssr'}) mustache).
roles: in app.yaml - when the tenant role name also appears under roles:, its scopes UNION into the session like any held role.

The OTHER tenant-role system (_benmore_user_roles with group_id - api({at:'rbac'})) composes with it: use role_field when the membership table is your source of truth (most collaboration apps), RBAC grants when you need expiring/auditable grants.
protected_columns: Generic CRUD (create, update, batch, ingest, /api/_transaction, revert, admin panel) never writes the role_field column of the groups membership table, admins included. With role_field set, an update can't change the identity column (groups.user_field) either: re-pointing a row hands its role to whoever the new value names, so the value is dropped like the role column. A new membership row may name any identity through a writable groups.user_field (an email column; a protected user_id takes only the caller, see membership_management → member_identity) and starts with the column's default role; who may create one is membership_management (a tenant admin unless the table declares its own rule). A user_field named user_id is protected: a create that names anyone but the caller answers 422 and creates nothing (membership_management → member_identity). Add members of such a table in a flow. Change a member's role or identity in a flow that checks who is asking.
duplicate_rows: A member with several live rows in one tenant gets the role of the oldest row (by rowid; a view or WITHOUT ROWID table orders by the role column), wherever the tenant role is read: session roles, workflow transition guards, SSR role sections and approved commands. The oldest row is also the one the tenant resolves from (membership_identity). benmore check and the post-write check warn when nothing makes (groups.key, groups.user_field) unique on the membership table: add @@unique([orgId, userId]), or, if removed members are soft-deleted and added again, a migration with a partial unique index (WHERE deleted_at IS NULL).
